# dgetc2

> Computes the LU factorization with complete pivoting of the general n-by-n matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgetc2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgetc2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgetc2( order, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, JPIV, strideJPIV ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A. |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the n-by-n matrix A to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization A = P\*L\*U\*Q; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · The pivot indices; for 1 <= i <= N, row i of the matrix has been interchanged with row IPIV(i) (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `JPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · The pivot indices; for 1 <= j <= N, column j of the matrix has been interchanged with column JPIV(j) (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideJPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `JPIV` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the n-by-n matrix A to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored. If U(k, k) appears to be less than SMIN, U(k, k) is given the value of SMIN, i.e., giving a nonsingular perturbed system.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix has been interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `JPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le j \le N$, column j of the matrix has been interchanged with column `JPIV(j)`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgetc2.ndarray(
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    JPIV, strideJPIV, offsetJPIV
) → info: integer
```

Performs LU factorization with complete pivoting of a general N-by-N matrix.

On exit, A contains the LU factors. IPIV(i) and JPIV(i) are the row and
column pivots applied at step i. INFO > 0 indicates that U(INFO,INFO) is
likely to produce overflow when used in dgesc2.

IPIV and JPIV are 0-based in this implementation.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · N-by-N matrix (overwritten with L and U) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Row pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IPIV |
| `JPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Column pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideJPIV` | `integer` | Stride for JPIV |
| ↳ `offsetJPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for JPIV |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the n-by-n matrix A to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored. If U(k, k) appears to be less than SMIN, U(k, k) is given the value of SMIN, i.e., giving a nonsingular perturbed system.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix has been interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `JPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le j \le N$, column j of the matrix has been interchanged with column `JPIV(j)`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if U(info,info) is small

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = k`, U(k, k) is likely to produce overflow if we try to solve for x in $\mathrm{Ax} = b$. So U is perturbed to avoid the overflow.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dgetc2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgetc2';

const N = 3;

// Column-major, nonsingular 3-by-3 matrix:
const A0 = [ 4.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 5.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 6.0 ];

// Using the standard interface:
let A = new Float64Array( A0 );
let IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
let JPIV = new Int32Array( N );
let out = dgetc2( 'column-major', N, A, N, IPIV, 1, JPIV, 1 );
console.log( out, A, IPIV, JPIV ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Float64Array( A0 );
IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
JPIV = new Int32Array( N );
out = dgetc2.ndarray( N, A, 1, N, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, JPIV, 1, 0 );
console.log( out, A, IPIV, JPIV ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGETC2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGETC2 computes an LU factorization with complete pivoting of the n-by-n matrix A. The factorization has the form $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$, where P and Q are permutation matrices, L is lower triangular with unit diagonal elements and U is upper triangular.

This is the Level 2 BLAS algorithm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
